questions.question: Explain a grid plate as it relates to aircraft leveling.
questions.idealAnswer: The grid plate is a permanent fixture installed on the aircraft floor or supporting structure. To level an aircraft, a plumb bob is suspended from a predetermined position in the celling of the aircraft over the grid plate. The adjustment's to the jacks necessary to level the aircraft are indicated on the grid scale. The aircraft is level when the plumb bob is suspended over the center of the grid.

questions.question: Define a progressive inspection.

This permits a steeper glided angle and lower speed to be obtained for the landing approach.

questions.question: What is a balance tab?
questions.idealAnswer: It is an auxiliary control with fixed linkage that is designed in such a way that when the primary control surface is moved the tab moves in the opposite direction. Aerodynamic forces (back pressure) acting on the tab assists the pilot in moving the control surface.

questions.question: What is a trim tab?
questions.idealAnswer: It is a n auxiliary control attached to the trailing edge of the primary control surface that is positioned by movement of a cockpit control to reduce the workload on the pilot in maintaining a desired flight attitude.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the collective pitch control in a helicopter?
questions.idealAnswer: It is used to change the pitch of the main rotor blades therefore increasing or decreasing lift.

questions.question: In relation to an aircraft, what is the boundary layer?

questions.question: Why is it important that the leading edge of supersonic aircraft wings be kept free from dents and damage?
questions.idealAnswer: Sharp leading edges allow oblique shock waves to attach to the wings in supersonic flight. If the leading edge has dents or blunt surfaces, a normal shockwave forms and slows the air behind it to subsonic. Oblique shock waves are incline angled to airflow direction; normal shock waves are perpendicular to airflow direction.
